q: How do I calculate the emissions of a multiple effect evaporator (MEE)?
title: Multiple effect evaporator emissions
short: Give the MEE its share of boiler fuel from the live steam it takes, add pump and vacuum electricity at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, and divide by kilolitres of effluent evaporated. More effects use less steam per kilolitre, so the steam meter shows how the MEE is performing.
audience: Textile, pharma, chemical and distillery units running MEEs for zero liquid discharge

ul: Live steam to the first effect.
An agitated dryer or ATFD after the MEE, if fitted.

p: Kilograms of water evaporated per kilogram of live steam is the MEE's steam economy. Track it monthly; scaling or a vacuum leak lowers it and raises fuel use.
The MEE runs on your boiler fuel (Scope 1) and grid power (Scope 2). Salts or sludge sent to a TSDF are waste in Scope 3.

example.title: Worked example: one month of MEE operation (illustrative inputs)
lines: Boiler PNG: 20,000 scm x 2.05 = 41,000 kg CO2 for 240 t steam
MEE live steam: 96 t steam of 240 = 40.0%
MEE pumps and vacuum: 7,000 kWh x 0.710 = 4,970 kg CO2
Total: 21,370 kg CO2 for 1,500 kL of effluent evaporated = 14.2 kg CO2 per kL
example.note: Fuel, steam and volume are illustrative; use the MEE steam meter and evaporation log.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 records. A per-unit figure divides those by the output you enter, and purchased materials are added from supplier data on the Scope 3 trail, labelled by source.
